transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because of work. It’s... dispatch and compliance. They’ve been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and they make these little comments on the radio. Which, actually, my rig's radio has been having this awful static lately, right around 2:00 PM every day. It sounds exactly like this old ham radio my grandfather used to keep out in his shed. He spent hours in that shed... he had all these glass jars of nails sorted by size. I used to help him organize them when I was little, just sitting on this overturned bucket. 

But, um, anyway, what was I... right, the tracking. People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, but I know it's not. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. Like Dave, who always brings those smelly boiled eggs to the breakroom. I really don't understand how someone can eat boiled eggs at 6 AM, it lingers in the whole terminal. But yeah, Dave and the others, they're definitely reporting on me to dispatch.
When you say people are reporting on you to dispatch, how certain are you about that? Is there any part of you that wonders if maybe you could be mistaken about it?

No, I'm not mistaken. I mean, I know people keep saying it’s just normal oversight, but I am completely certain. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me, and dispatch and compliance are definitely tracking my route changes right there through the computer system. It’s obvious when you hear those little comments on the radio. 

Which... the radio in my rig is a Motorola, I think. Or maybe it's a Kenwood? My dad had a Kenwood stereo system in our living room growing up. Huge speakers, like, they came all the way up to my waist. He’d play Fleetwood Mac on Sunday mornings while making pancakes. He always burnt the first pancake, every single time. He said the cast iron pan just needed to warm up, but I think he just had the burner turned up way too high. I haven't had pancakes in forever, actually. The diner near the depot serves them, but the syrup is that fake corn syrup stuff, you know? It just coats your teeth and leaves this weird film. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Right, about being sure. No, I'm definitely not mistaken about them tracking me. It's really happening.

If I told you that I checked with your dispatch office and they said the radio comments are just routine operational chatter and there's no special tracking of your route, would that change your mind at all, or would you still believe they're reporting on you?

No, it wouldn't change my mind at all, because I know what's actually happening. If you called the dispatch office, they’re obviously just going to tell you it’s routine operational chatter to cover it up. You probably talked to Brenda, right? She sits at this huge curved desk up front. The laminate on the edge of her desk is all peeling off and you can see the particle board underneath. My apartment kitchen counter was peeling exactly like that when I first moved in. The landlord promised he’d replace it, but he just painted over it with this thick, sticky beige gloss. It took weeks to dry properly. If you set a coffee mug down, it would just stick to the paint and leave a ring. I had this one mug, it had a picture of a cartoon cat on it that changed color when you poured hot water in... I got it at a thrift store in Portland. Portland has the best thrift stores, honestly. You can find all sorts of vintage stuff there. I bought a green corduroy jacket once that had a movie ticket from 1993 still folded up in the pocket. 

But... wait, sorry. What was I saying about the office? Oh, right. No, it really doesn't matter what dispatch tells you. Even when people say it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. Compliance is absolutely tracking my route changes through the computer system, and those little comments on the radio are real. I know what I hear, so them denying it doesn't change anything.

How long have you been having these concerns about people reporting on you and dispatch tracking your routes? And have you been able to keep working as a truck driver this whole time without any problems, or has this situation gotten in the way of your job recently?

The tracking through the computer system and those radio comments... it's all felt really clear to me for about the past two months. I know it's been two months because it started right around the time I bought this new air freshener for my cab. It was shaped like a little tree and supposed to smell like "Pine Forest," but it honestly just smelled like cheap bathroom cleaner. You know that industrial cleaner they use in the rest stop bathrooms? The one that's aggressively lemon-scented but still somehow smells like wet dirt? 

I really hate stopping at the rest areas on Interstate 80. The vending machines are always broken. Last time I put a dollar in, it just ate my money and didn't even give me my Cheetos. I love Cheetos, but only the crunchy ones. The puffs just get stuck in the roof of your mouth and you have to use your tongue to scrape them off for like ten minutes. My roommate when I was getting my associate's degree used to eat the puffs with chopsticks so she wouldn't get the orange dust on her keyboard. She was an accounting major, always typing on this loud mechanical keyboard late at night. The clicking sound used to drive me crazy when I was trying to study... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. What were you asking me? Oh, right, about work. If it's getting in the way. I mean, I'm still driving. I haven't missed any shifts or anything. I just keep my head down and do my routes, even though I know exactly what they're doing.
When you hear those comments on the radio from dispatch, are you hearing actual words and voices, or are you interpreting the static and routine chatter as if it's directed at you?

I'm hearing actual voices. Actual words. It's not static. Like, I hear the other drivers and dispatch talking, and I know they're talking about me. The radio is pretty clear most of the time, unless I'm going through the mountains. 

When you go through the pass near Snoqualmie, the signal completely drops out. It's actually kind of nice, just having the quiet. I usually listen to audiobooks when I lose the radio signal. I was listening to this one mystery novel about a detective in a small coastal town, but the narrator did this really weird voice for all the female characters. It sounded like he was pinching his nose while he talked. I couldn't even finish it. I ended up returning it on the app. The app is actually pretty great, you just connect your library card and you can borrow anything. My local library back home was this beautiful old brick building with huge arched windows. I used to go there after school and sit in the reference section because it was the only place with air conditioning in the summer. The librarian was this older woman who always wore these brightly colored, chunky beaded necklaces. They would clack against the desk when she stamped the books...

Um... wait. What were we talking about? The radio? Yeah, no, it's definitely actual words I'm hearing. It's not just static or whatever. I know what they're saying.
When you hear these actual words and voices on the radio talking about you, do they ever tell you to do something, or do they just make comments about you?

They don't really tell me to do things. It's more like they're just commenting on me. Like, they'll say things about my route or what I'm doing in the cab. Just talking about me, you know? 

It's kind of like when you're at a restaurant and you can hear the people in the booth behind you talking about their food, but you know they're actually talking about how you eat your salad. I always get the Cobb salad at this one diner off Route 66. They put way too much blue cheese on it, though. I like blue cheese, but it can be really overpowering if you're not careful. I tried making my own blue cheese dressing once at home. I bought this fancy wedge of Roquefort from a cheese shop downtown. The shop smelled amazing, like aged cheddar and fresh sourdough bread. The guy working there had this incredible handlebar mustache, like an old-timey bartender. He told me he waxed it every morning. I can't imagine spending that much time on a mustache. My brother tried to grow a mustache for Movember last year, but it just came in all patchy and weird. He looked like a teenager trying to buy beer. He ended up shaving it off before Thanksgiving because our mom kept making fun of him. She makes this really dry turkey every year, no matter what recipe she tries...

Sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the radio. No, they don't give me commands or anything like that. Just comments.

When you hear these voices and comments on the radio about you, if I were sitting right there in your cab with you listening to the same radio, would I hear those exact same words and voices, or would I just hear normal dispatch chatter?

If you were sitting right there... well, you'd probably say exactly what everyone else says. People always tell me it's just normal oversight, just regular dispatch chatter. But I know what's going on. I know dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and they use those little comments on the radio to do it. 

I don't usually have anyone riding in the cab with me anyway. The company has a really strict policy about unauthorized passengers. I was thinking about getting a dog to ride with me, though, maybe a Jack Russell terrier. My neighbor growing up had one named Buster, and that dog had so much energy he actually chewed straight through their wooden fence. Just gnawed right through the pine planks. Wood is so ridiculously expensive right now, too. I went to the hardware store last month to get a simple shelf for my apartment, and I couldn't believe the price for just a basic piece of plywood. The guy working in the lumber aisle wasn't even helping anyone, he was just leaning against a forklift watching videos on his phone of people making these giant, oversized pancakes on a griddle. I don't even know how you'd flip a pancake that big without breaking it, you'd need two spatulas or maybe like a pizza peel...

Wait, sorry. The radio. Right. So even if you were there and thought it was just regular chatter, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. They're definitely reporting me to compliance. You might not pick up on it right away, but I know exactly what they're doing.

Let me ask this more directly: When you hear those voices and comments on the radio about you, are you hearing something that's actually coming through the radio speaker, or are you hearing voices in your head that no one else can hear?

I don't really get what you mean by that. It sounds like it's coming right out of the speaker. The speaker in my cab is actually pretty new, I had to replace the factory ones last year because the driver's side kept crackling every time someone talked too loud. I took it to this audio shop in Spokane, and the guy who worked there had this massive collection of vintage radios in the lobby. Like, those huge wooden cabinet ones from the 1930s. He said his grandfather used to listen to the Lone Ranger on them. I always thought it would be kind of cool to live back then, you know, just riding horses everywhere instead of driving. 

I went horseback riding once when I was ten for my friend Sarah's birthday party. The horse they gave me was named Barnaby, and he was so stubborn, he just kept trying to eat the bushes instead of walking on the trail. Sarah actually ended up crying because her horse stepped in a huge mud puddle and completely ruined her jeans. They were those really trendy ones with the little rhinestones on the back pockets, everyone had them in middle school and they were super expensive... 

Um, wait. What did you ask? Oh, in my head? No, I don't think they're just in my head. Like I said, I hear them when the radio is on. I'm not just making it up.

I want to be very clear about this: When you hear dispatch talking about you on the radio, if I recorded what was coming out of that speaker and played it back later, would the words about you be on that recording, or would only the normal dispatch chatter be on it?

If you recorded it? I don't know, I've never tried to record it. I guess if you used your phone or something... My phone's microphone is actually broken right now, every time I try to leave a voice memo it just sounds like I'm underwater. I dropped it in a puddle outside the grocery store last week. It was pouring rain, just absolutely dumping, and this guy in front of me had a cart full of those giant bags of dog food and one ripped open, kibble everywhere. The seagulls swooped down immediately. Have you ever noticed how aggressive seagulls are getting lately? I saw one steal a whole sandwich right out of a kid's hand at the beach last summer. The kid screamed so loud, his mom had to buy him ice cream to calm him down. They got mint chocolate chip, which is my favorite, but I can't eat it anymore because I'm lactose intolerant. I tried those dairy-free ones made with oat milk, but they always have this weird aftertaste, kind of like cardboard... 

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. You were asking about a recording? I really don't know what would be on the tape. I just know what I hear when I'm driving.

When you're listening to the radio in your cab and you hear dispatch talking about you, do other people who are listening to that same radio at dispatch headquarters or in other trucks hear those exact same words about you, or do you think only you can hear what's being said about you?

Well, I think they hear the exact same things, but like I told you, they just say it's normal oversight. The other drivers hear those little comments on the radio, they just play dumb. Truckers can be really secretive anyway. I met this one guy at a weigh station outside Boise who had his entire cab decorated with velvet Elvis paintings. He said he bought them all at this huge flea market down in Memphis. I've never been to Tennessee, but I really love country music. Dolly Parton is probably my favorite. Did you know she actually wrote 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You' on the exact same day? That's just crazy productivity. Whenever I try to get things done on my days off, I just end up reorganizing my kitchen cabinets. I bought all these clear plastic bins to sort my pantry, but now I can't remember where I put the lid to my favorite travel mug. It's stainless steel and keeps my coffee hot for like twelve hours, which you really need on long hauls... 

Um, anyway. You were asking who else hears it? Yeah, I mean, the other people at headquarters or in their trucks definitely hear it. But even when people say it's just normal oversight, I know the truth. Dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and I can tell certain drivers are the ones reporting on me using those comments. So they hear it, they just won't admit what they're actually doing.

When you're driving and hear dispatch on the radio talking about you, and you listen very carefully to exactly what words they're saying — are you certain those specific words about you are actually being broadcast, or is it possible you're picking up on something vague in the static or routine chatter and interpreting it as being about you?

Am I certain? Yeah, I'm absolutely certain. It’s definitely not just static or me misinterpreting things. I know exactly what's going on. Dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and they use those little comments on the radio to do it. 

Speaking of the computer system, they upgraded our software a few months ago and it is such a pain to use. I actually had to get a new laptop for myself at home because my old one completely died right around the same time. I spilled a whole cup of green tea right onto the keyboard. It was that matcha kind, you know? My sister got me super into matcha when she came back from her trip to Japan last spring. She brought back all these amazing snacks, like those KitKats that are green tea flavored, and these little rice crackers wrapped in seaweed. Seaweed is actually super good for you, it has a lot of iodine or something. I tried to make homemade sushi once after she visited, but the rice got way too sticky and it just turned into a giant mushy bowl. I ended up just eating it with a spoon while watching this documentary about deep-sea squids. Did you know some squids can glow in the dark? It's called bioluminescence. They use it to confuse predators, which is honestly so smart... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, the static. Right. No, it's not static. Because even when people say it’s just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I hear the exact words they're saying, so I know I'm not just picking up on vague chatter.
